To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression and the enzymatic activity of APN and of DPIV are regulated by T‐cell‐derived cytokines.

IL‐4, IL‐13, IL‐1β, and TNF‐α increase the expression and enzyme activities of aminopeptide N (APN)/CD13 and diptepidylpeptide IV (DPIV)/CD26 on human kidney carcinoma cells and renal epithelial cells in vitro, whereas IFN‐γ and TGF‐β1 have an inhibitory effect.
IL‐4 up‐regulates the expression and the activity of the peptidase APN and DPIIV on renal carcinoma cells, whereas TGF‐β1 down‐regulates DPIV.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of ectopeptidae expression and activity on renal carcinoma cells by cytokines.
the effects of T cell‐derived and non‐T cell‐derived cytokine on the expression of APN and DPIV on tumour cells and normal renal cells in vitro.

the regulation of the two peptidases APN and DPIY by cytokines on renal carcinoma cells, and the data obtained are of importance for the understanding of the biological function of the two peptylases on renal cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression and enzyme activities of APN and DIPV can be regulated by cytokines.
the regulation of APNs and DPIVs on tumour cells is complex and that the cytokine‐mediated regulation of ectopeptidasess may be an important aspect in the development of tumour cell metastases.

cytokines may be used as a tool in the therapy of renal cell carcinoma, but their use should be restricted to a combination with other therapeutic approaches, such as surgery, chemotherapy, or radiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL‐4, IL‐13 and IFN‐γ are able to increase the protein expression of APN and to a lesser extent that of DPIV.
IL‐4 is a cytokine which is able to stimulate the expression and enzymatic activity of APN and to a lesser extent of DPIV on human renal cell carcinomas.

the regulation of the expression and enzyme activities of APN and especially DPIV by T cell‐ derived cytokines is a complex process and might be of importance for the development of a tumour cell metastatic phenotype.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cytokines IL‐4 and IFN‐γ can up‐regulation the expression and enzyme activities of APN and DPPV in human renal cell carcinoma cell lines.
IL‐4, IL‐13 and IL‐1β are able to increase the protein expression and enzyme activity on APN and, at least in part, also on DPIV of renal cell carcinoma cells.

the cytokines IL‐4 and IFN‐γ can increase protein expression of APN and/or DPIV on renal tumour cells, and IL‐4, IFN‐γ, and TNF‐a can increase enzyme activity of APN and of IL‐4 and TNF‐α can also increase enzyme activity of DPIIV.
